blocks.text: SAN FRANCISCO, Agusan del Sur — Does an indigent patient need a congressman’s face on a piece of paper to get treatment? A Surigao del Sur lawyer is demanding answers from health and state audit officials over referral slips carrying the portrait and name of 1st District Rep. Romeo Momo Sr.—documents the lawmaker claims his staff may have circulated without his knowledge or signature. In an open letter posted on social media, Atty. Mary Helen Zafra challenged Momo, the Department of Health (DOH), the Commission on Audit (COA), and local executives to clarify whether political endorsements are an institutional requirement or […]...
